package_info.package_versions: N/A (APT campaign, not a public package)
package_info.why_malicious: ThreatNeedle is a custom malware family used by the North Korean APT Lazarus group to target defense industry entities. It is designed for espionage, leveraging spear-phishing with Covid-19 themes and tailored personal information to gain initial access, then performing data exfiltration and lateral movement.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom malware binary (ThreatNeedle) that, once executed, establishes a C2 channel, enumerates files, and exfiltrates data.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a command-and-control (C2) connection to a remote server, enumerates files and directories, and exfiltrates selected data to the attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing a C2 channel and exfiltrating files is a hallmark of targeted espionage malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not open persistent outbound connections to unknown servers or exfiltrate sensitive files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may have similar capabilities, but only with explicit user consent and to trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Outbound C2 traffic to suspicious infrastructure
Execution of dropped binaries from spear-phishing emails

execution_context.file_location: malicious document or executable attached to spear-phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Covid-19 themed spear-phishing document with embedded macro or exploit that drops and executes ThreatNeedle payload.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the malicious attachment, the embedded macro or exploit executes, dropping the ThreatNeedle malware binary to disk and launching it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malicious macros or exploits in documents are a common initial access vector for APT campaigns.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documents should not contain macros or exploits that drop and execute binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Macros may be used for automation in business documents, but not for dropping executables.
key_indicators: Dropping and executing binaries from documents

attack_chain.action: Victim receives spear-phishing email with Covid-19 themed attachment containing malicious macro or exploit.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of ThreatNeedle malware on victim machine

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro or exploit executes, dropping and launching the ThreatNeedle malware binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of C2 channel and data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: ThreatNeedle malware establishes C2 connection, enumerates files, and exfiltrates data to attacker infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of macros or exploits from Covid-19 themed documents
Dropping and execution of unknown binaries from document context
Outbound C2 connections to suspicious or known APT infrastructure
file_indicators: Covid-19 themed document attachments with embedded macros
Dropped executables with uncommon or random filenames
Persistence mechanisms created by unknown binaries
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Lazarus/ThreatNeedle C2 domains or IPs
Unusual traffic patterns to remote servers after document opening
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of macros or exploits in document attachments, especially those with Covid-19 themes. Detect dropped and executed binaries originating from document processes. Analyze outbound network traffic for connections to known APT infrastructure or anomalous destinations. Use endpoint detection to flag automated file enumeration and exfiltration behaviors.
